text: A script that only runs when someone remembers isn't automation. Mara schedules the Lesson 8 script as an Azure Automation Runbook, authenticating through a system-assigned managed identity with no stored secret at all, running daily at 3 a.m. UTC with a read-only scope -- enough to report on access, with no ability to change it.

Before trusting the output, Mara runs a deliberate test case. The AWS team attaches the SCADA Emergency Access policy directly to a disposable test account, without adding it to the scada-ot-admins group. Running the script should surface that test account with access_path set to direct assignment -- direct proof the script catches exactly the kind of access a group-only review would miss.

After detaching the policy, a re-run should show the test account gone entirely. And running the script twice with no changes in between should produce identical output both times, confirming idempotency -- essential for a script that will run unattended, every day, with no one watching it.

With the test case passed and failures set to alert on-call instead of failing silently, the runbook goes live. ScadaAccessInventory_CL now refreshes every morning with no manual step. Next lesson turns this running inventory into the first real input for Hartwell's formal GRC risk register.
